Owen and Mia are preparing a report about the ticket office. Mia will take part in a badminton match in January. Mia has practiced badminton for three years and won a prize last term. The hotel room has a sea view.

They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. The bus stop has become an important part of daily life. Mia believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. Also, archives keep the original blueprints.
There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. The experience taught Mia more than any book could. Mia wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Traffic banks up before the flyover.

On Sunday evenings, Mia reviews the notes from class. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Best of all, a snapped tent pole splinted with tape.
At first, Mia found it difficult to keep the habit. Little by little, things began to change. Mia thanked Owen for the honest advice.
